q: 补全 DynamoDB 的三个关键词定位：
q_en: Fill in DynamoDB's three positioning keywords:
text: DynamoDB 是 AWS 提供的{{全托管}}（AWS 负责硬件、配置、打补丁、扩缩容）、{{高可扩展}}（自动扩缩、无停机）、{{键值}}模型的 NoSQL 数据库服务。
why: 三个 buzzword 各有实义：全托管=运维外包给 AWS，高可扩展=自动伸缩无性能退化，键值=非关系模型、存取灵活。
why_en: DynamoDB is a fully managed, highly scalable key-value NoSQL service where AWS handles all operations and scaling automatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库统称，不强制固定的表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL refers to non-relational databases that do not require a fixed table schema.

termDefinitions.meaning: 亚马逊云服务，DynamoDB 的运营方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS, Amazon Web Services, is the cloud provider that operates DynamoDB.

q: 过去对 DynamoDB 最大的批评之一是什么？现在情况如何？
q_en: What used to be one of the biggest criticisms of DynamoDB, and how does that stand today?
options: 不支持事务——现已支持 ACID 事务
不能存储 JSON 嵌套结构——现在仍然不能
无法水平扩展到大规模——现在仍然如此
没有任何一致性保证——至今仍无可选项
why: 「NoSQL 没有事务」的老论调对 DynamoDB 已经不成立：它通过 TransactWriteItems / TransactGetItems 支持跨表 ACID 事务。
why_en: DynamoDB now supports ACID transactions, neutralizing the old criticism that NoSQL means no transactions.
options_en: It used to lack transactions, but now it supports ACID transactions.
It cannot store nested JSON structures -- and still cannot today.
It cannot scale horizontally to large workloads -- still true today.
It offers no consistency guarantees at all, with no options to choose from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库事务的四个安全属性：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID describes the four safety guarantees a transaction provides: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的多项原子写入 API，跨表提供可串行化隔离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TransactWriteItems is DynamoDB's API for committing multiple writes atomically across tables with serializable isolation.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的多项原子读取 API，在一次事务里读取多个 item。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TransactGetItems reads multiple items together as a single atomic transaction.

scenario: 面试官对 DynamoDB 抛出「NoSQL 没有事务」的老印象。
scenario_en: The interviewer brings up the old view that 'NoSQL means no transactions' about DynamoDB.
optionExplanations: 这是唯一站得住脚的说法：老批评曾经真实，但现在已经被事务 API 补上了。
JSON 只是传输格式，item 的 attribute 本身早就支持嵌套结构，这个说法站不住。
auto-sharding 正是它的卖点，扩展性从来不是短板，这个说法说反了。
它其实有最终一致和强一致两档可选，不是完全没有保证。
optionExplanations_en: This is the only one that holds up: the old complaint was once true, but transaction APIs closed that gap.
JSON is just the transport format -- attributes have always supported nested structures, so this claim fails.
Auto-sharding is its selling point, not a weakness, so this reverses reality.
It actually offers a choice between eventual and strong consistency, not zero guarantees.

q: 补全 DynamoDB 的数据层级：
q_en: Fill in DynamoDB's data hierarchy:
text: DynamoDB 数据层级：{{Table}}（顶层结构，必须定义主键，支持二级索引）→ {{Item}}（相当于关系库的行，单条上限 {{400KB}}）→ {{Attribute}}（键值对，支持标量、集合和嵌套类型）。
why: Table/Item/Attribute 对应关系库的表/行/列，但 item 有 400KB 大小上限、attribute 可以嵌套，模型为扩展性和灵活性做了取舍。
why_en: Tables hold items, which are like rows capped at four hundred kilobytes, made of attributes that can be scalar, set, or nested types.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    Table["Table"] --> Item["Item"]
    Item --> Attr["Attributes"]
    Item --> PK["partition key"]
    Item --> SK["optional sort key"]

q: DynamoDB 是 schema-less（无模式）的，这带来什么直接后果？
q_en: DynamoDB is schema-less -- what's the direct consequence of that?
options: 同一张表里所有 item 都必须携带完全相同的属性集合
写入前必须先在建表时声明所有列的类型
不同 item 可以有不同属性，应用层负责校验。
完全无法建立任何索引
why: 无模式带来高灵活性：不同 item 属性可不同、新属性随加随用；代价是 DynamoDB 不强制属性一致性，应用必须自己做数据校验。
why_en: Being schema-less lets items in one table carry different attributes, but pushes data validation responsibility onto the application.
options_en: Every item in one table must carry exactly the same set of attributes.
You must declare every column's type at table creation before writing.
Items can carry different attributes, and validation is the application's job.
No index of any kind can ever be built.
optionExplanations: 无模式恰恰相反：item 之间的属性完全可以不同，不存在强制统一。
这是关系库的建表思路，DynamoDB 插入前不用声明任何列。
灵活是有代价的：类型/必填这些校验全靠应用层自己兜底，DynamoDB 不拦截。
无模式不等于没索引，主键索引、GSI、LSI 照样能建。
optionExplanations_en: Schema-less means the opposite -- items can carry completely different attributes, nothing is forced uniform.
That's the relational mindset; DynamoDB needs no column declared before an insert.
The flexibility has a price: type and presence checks are entirely the application's job, since DynamoDB won't enforce them.
Schema-less doesn't mean indexless -- the primary key index, GSIs, and LSIs still work fine.
scenario: 给一个商品目录表建模，不同品类的属性差异很大，且新属性要随时能加。
scenario_en: You're modeling a product catalog where categories carry very different attributes and new ones get added constantly.

q: DynamoDB 用 JSON 收发数据，说明它内部也以 JSON 格式存储吗？
q_en: DynamoDB sends and receives data as JSON -- does that mean it's stored as JSON internally too?
options: 是，磁盘上直接以 JSON 文本文件的形式逐条存储
JSON 只是传输格式，存储格式是专有的。
内部存储是 XML
内部存储是 CSV
why: JSON 仅仅是 API 层的传输格式；底层存储格式是 AWS 专有实现，这让用户可以专注数据建模而不用管物理存储。
why_en: JSON is only the transport format, while DynamoDB's actual storage format is proprietary and abstracted away from users.
options_en: Yes -- on disk it is stored directly as line-by-line JSON text files.
JSON is only the transport format; the storage format is proprietary.
Internally DynamoDB stores data as XML.
Internally DynamoDB stores data as CSV.
scenario: 同事看到 DynamoDB 用 JSON 收发数据，就以为底层也是这么存的。
scenario_en: A coworker sees DynamoDB using JSON for requests and responses and assumes that's also the storage format underneath.
optionExplanations: 这是把 API 收发格式和磁盘落盘格式搞混了，两者不是一回事。
两层要分开看：接口收发用 JSON，落盘用的是 AWS 自己的专有格式，用户不用操心。
没有证据支持 XML 这个猜测，AWS 从未这样描述过存储层。
CSV 同样是没有依据的猜测，纯文本格式也不适合它的检索需求。
optionExplanations_en: This confuses the API's send/receive format with what's actually written to disk -- they aren't the same thing.
Split the two layers: the API speaks JSON, but storage uses AWS's own proprietary format that users never touch.
There's no evidence for XML -- AWS never describes the storage layer that way.
CSV is an equally baseless guess, and plain text wouldn't fit its lookup needs anyway.

q: DynamoDB 的 partition key 起什么作用？
q_en: What role does the partition key play in DynamoDB?
options: 决定同一分区内 item 的排序与展示顺序
仅用于对 item 内容做静态加密
限制单个 item 能保存的最大字节数
哈希定位物理分区，并组成主键
why: partition key 哈希后决定数据的物理位置，是数据分布和查询效率的根基；加上可选的 sort key 组成主键唯一标识每个 item。
why_en: The partition key's value is hashed to determine which physical partition stores the item, and with the sort key it uniquely identifies the item.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Q["Request with partition key"] --> H["hash key"]
    H --> M["partition map"]
    M --> P["storage partition"]
    P --> B["sort key lookup"]
options_en: It determines the sort and display order of items inside one partition.
It is used only to encrypt an item's contents at rest.
It caps the maximum byte size of a single item.
Its hash locates the physical partition, and it forms part of the primary key.
scenario: 设计一张表要先确定主键，partition key 是主键的第一部分。
scenario_en: Designing a table starts with choosing a primary key, and the partition key is the first part of it.
optionExplanations: 分区内的排序其实是 sort key 的活，真正管辖分区归属的是 partition key。
加密和分区键无关，静态数据加密是 AWS 默认处理的另一件事。
400KB 的 item 大小上限是固定值，跟分区键怎么选没关系。
分区键的哈希值决定数据落在哪个物理分区，再靠 sort key 补齐成完整的复合主键。
optionExplanations_en: Ordering within a partition is the sort key's job; the partition key only decides which partition an item lands in.
Encryption has nothing to do with the partition key -- encryption at rest is a separate default AWS handles.
The 400KB item size cap is a fixed limit, unrelated to how the partition key is chosen.
Its hash determines the physical partition, and together with the sort key it forms the full primary key.

q: sort key 的作用是？
q_en: What is the sort key's role?
options: 在同一分区内排序 item，支持范围查询
决定数据落在哪个 AWS region
决定该表的副本数量
自动为每个 item 打时间戳
why: sort key 可选：有了它才能做分区内的范围查询和排序（如按时间取一段消息），它和 partition key 一起构成复合主键。
why_en: The optional sort key orders items sharing a partition key, enabling efficient range queries and sorting within a partition.
options_en: It orders items that share a partition key, enabling range queries within a partition.
It determines which AWS region the data lands in.
It determines how many replicas the table has.
It automatically stamps every item with a timestamp.
optionExplanations: 它和分区键一起组成复合主键，让同一分区内的数据可以按顺序范围检索。
region 是建表时选的部署位置，跟排序键完全是两件事。
副本数固定是 3，由 AWS 统一管理，不是靠键设计调整的。
排序键的值要应用显式写入，DynamoDB 不会替你自动生成时间戳。
optionExplanations_en: Paired with the partition key it forms the composite primary key, letting items in one partition be range-queried in order.
Region is chosen when the table is created, entirely separate from sort key design.
Replica count is a fixed three, managed by AWS -- key design has no say in it.
A sort key's value must be written explicitly by the app; DynamoDB never auto-stamps it.
scenario: 设计聊天表，要按 chat_id 取「最近 50 条消息」这样的时间范围查询。
scenario_en: You're designing a chat table and need to pull the latest 50 messages for a chat as a time range.

scenario: 做一个群聊应用：最常见的查询是「取某个群的所有消息并按时间排序展示」。
scenario_en: Building a group chat app: the most common query is 'fetch all messages for a chat, sorted by time.'
q: 主键应该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the primary key be designed?
options: partition key = message_id
partition key = user_id，sort key = message_id
partition key = chat_id，sort key = message_id
partition key = timestamp
why: 按 chat_id 分区让一个群的消息聚在一起，一次 Query 即可取出；单调递增的 message_id 作 sort key 提供时间顺序。分区键永远围绕最常见查询模式选。
why_en: Partitioning by chat id with a monotonically increasing message id sort key lets one query fetch a chat's messages in chronological order.
whenOtherWins: 若最常见查询是「某用户跨群的全部消息」，那 user_id 才是合适的分区维度——可用 GSI 补充。
options_en: Partition key equals message id.
Partition key equals user id, sort key equals message id.
Partition key equals chat id, sort key equals message id.
Partition key equals timestamp.
tradeoff: 按群聚合读取 vs 按用户聚合读取
optionExplanations: 以消息自身 ID 分区会把同一个群的消息打散到各个分区，取群消息时没法聚合。
这套键设计服务的是「查某用户跨群的所有消息」，本题要的是按群查，维度选错了。
按群聚合是本题的核心查询，chat_id 分区把一个群的消息聚在一起，message_id 排序天然给出时间顺序。
时间戳作为分区键既不对应任何真实聚合维度，还会让写入集中在少数时间窗口造成热点。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning by the message's own id scatters one chat's messages across partitions, so fetching a chat gives no aggregation.
This key design serves 'fetch one user's messages across chats' -- this scenario needs per-chat, so the dimension is wrong.
Per-chat aggregation is exactly what's needed here: chat_id groups a chat's messages together, and message_id gives chronological order for free.
Timestamp as a partition key maps to no real aggregation dimension and would concentrate writes into hot time windows.

scenario: 消息表的 sort key 需要既能按时间排序、又能唯一标识每条消息，候选是时间戳或单调递增 ID。
scenario_en: The message table's sort key needs to both order by time and uniquely identify each message; the candidates are a timestamp or a monotonically increasing id.
q: 为什么选单调递增 ID 而不是时间戳？
q_en: Why choose a monotonically increasing id over a timestamp?
options: 毫秒时间戳字段本身占用的存储空间比单调 ID 大得多
同一毫秒可能重复，单调 ID 保证顺序且唯一。
时间戳无法排序
DynamoDB 完全不支持任何数字类型
why: 排序键参与主键就必须唯一，毫秒级时间戳仍可能碰撞；单调递增 ID（UUID v7、Snowflake、ULID 等）一箭双雕：可排序 + 唯一。
why_en: Timestamps can collide within the same millisecond, while a monotonically increasing ID gives both chronological order and uniqueness.
whenOtherWins: 若该属性不参与主键、只做展示或粗粒度过滤，普通时间戳就够用。
options_en: A millisecond timestamp field itself takes far more storage than a monotonic id.
It can repeat within the same millisecond, while a monotonic id guarantees both order and uniqueness.
A timestamp cannot be sorted.
DynamoDB does not support numeric types at all.
tradeoff: 唯一性 + 可排序 vs 实现简单的裸时间戳
optionExplanations: 时间戳和单调 ID 通常都只占几到十几字节，空间从来不是决定因素。
排序键要参与主键就必须唯一，同一毫秒的并发写会让裸时间戳撞车，单调 ID 才能同时给出顺序和唯一性。
时间戳数值本身完全可比较排序，问题从不在排序能力，而在唯一性。
Number 是 DynamoDB 的基础标量类型之一，这个前提本身就是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Timestamps and monotonic ids both take only a handful of bytes -- space was never the deciding factor.
A sort key that's part of the primary key must be unique, and same-millisecond writes can collide on a bare timestamp; a monotonic id gives order and uniqueness together.
A timestamp value is perfectly sortable on its own -- the real problem is uniqueness, not sorting.
Number is one of DynamoDB's basic scalar types, so this premise is simply false.

q: 哪些是生成「可按时间排序且唯一」ID 的常见技术？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are common techniques for generating ids that are both time-sortable and unique? (select all)
options: 每分区自增计数器
UUID v7
Snowflake ID
ULID
随机 UUID v4
why: 前四种都能给出时间有序且唯一的 ID；UUID v4 是纯随机的，唯一但不可按时间排序，不满足需求。
why_en: Per-partition counters, UUID v7, snowflake IDs, and ULIDs all provide sortable unique IDs, unlike random UUID v4.
options_en: A per-partition auto-incrementing counter.
UUID v7.
Snowflake ID.
ULID.
A random UUID v4.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用唯一标识符；v7 时间戳在前可排序，v1 含 MAC 地址会泄露信息，v4 纯随机不可排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID is a universally unique identifier; version 7 is time-ordered and sortable, version 1 embeds the MAC address, and version 4 is purely random.

termDefinitions.meaning: Twitter 提出的分布式 ID 方案：时间戳+机器号+序列号拼接，天然有序且唯一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Snowflake ID combines a timestamp, machine id, and sequence number into a sortable, unique identifier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 字典序可排序的唯一标识符，时间戳编码在前缀里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ULID is a unique identifier that sorts lexicographically because its timestamp is encoded in the prefix.

optionExplanations: 分区内严格递增，能保证同一分区里的排序和唯一性，但不保证跨分区全局有序。
时间戳编码在最前面，字符串字典序就是时间序，还不像 v1 那样暴露 MAC 地址。
拼上机器号和序列号，多节点并发生成也不会撞车，天然全局有序。
时间戳编码进前缀、字典序可排序，常以 26 位 Base32 字符串呈现。
纯随机生成不带任何时间信息，字典序和时间毫无关系，满足不了可排序的要求。
optionExplanations_en: Strictly increasing within a partition, guaranteeing order and uniqueness there, though not global cross-partition order.
The timestamp sits up front, so string ordering equals time ordering, without leaking a MAC address the way v1 does.
Combining a machine id with a sequence number avoids collisions across concurrent generators and stays globally ordered.
The timestamp is encoded in the prefix, sorting lexicographically, typically rendered as a 26-character Base32 string.
Purely random with no time information at all, so its lexicographic order has nothing to do with time -- it fails the sortability requirement.
scenario: 多台应用服务器并发写同一张事件表，主键要全局唯一且能按时间排序取最近记录。
scenario_en: Many app servers write one event table concurrently; keys must be globally unique and sortable by time to read the newest rows.

q: 为什么 UUID v7 比 UUID v1 更受推荐？
q_en: Why is UUID v7 preferred over UUID v1?
options: v7 生成的字符串编码比 v1 短，所以更受欢迎
v1 的时间戳精度不够，无法用于排序
v7 时间戳前置、字符串可排序，且不暴露 MAC 地址
v7 是 AWS 给 DynamoDB 定制的专有 ID 格式
why: UUID v7 把时间戳放在最前面，字符串字典序即时间序；同时它不含 MAC 地址，避免了 v1 的隐私泄露问题。
why_en: UUID v7 puts the timestamp first so it sorts naturally as a string and avoids exposing the machine's MAC address like v1 does.
options_en: v7 produces a shorter encoded string, which is why it became more popular.
v1's timestamp precision is too coarse to sort by.
v7 puts the timestamp first so it sorts naturally as a string, and it does not expose the machine's MAC address.
v7 is an AWS-proprietary id format built for DynamoDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用唯一标识符；v7 时间戳在前可排序，v1 含 MAC 地址会泄露信息，v4 纯随机不可排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID is a universally unique identifier; version 7 is time-ordered and sortable, version 1 embeds the MAC address, and version 4 is purely random.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网卡的硬件物理地址；UUID v1 会把它编码进 ID 造成信息泄露。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A MAC address is a network card's hardware identifier; UUID v1 embeds it in the id, leaking information.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新版 UUID(RFC 9562):开头 48 位是「大端 Unix 毫秒时间戳」、后面随机。所以①按字符串/字节排序=按生成时间排序②不含 MAC 地址。是数据库主键的现代推荐
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UUID v7 (RFC 9562): the first 48 bits are a big-endian Unix-millisecond timestamp, the rest random — so it sorts by creation time as a string/bytes and contains no MAC address. The modern recommendation for DB keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 时间戳 + MAC 地址 + 时钟序。两个毛病:①时间戳被拆成低/中/高段、顺序错乱 → 字符串排序≠时间序;②嵌了机器的 MAC 地址 → 泄露是哪台机器生成的(隐私/安全)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UUID v1: timestamp + MAC address + clock sequence. Two flaws: the timestamp is split into low/mid/high fields out of order, so string sort ≠ time order; and it embeds the machine MAC address, leaking which machine generated it.

termDefinitions.meaning: ID 按时间排序 → 顺序插入都落在索引「末尾」→ 索引/B树局部性好、少页分裂和碎片、插入快;还能按时间范围查询。随机 ID(如 v4)到处散 → 局部性差、碎片多。这正是 v7 相比全随机 v4 的价值
termDefinitions.meaningEn: When IDs sort by time, sequential inserts land at the end of the index → good B-tree locality, fewer page splits/fragmentation, faster inserts, plus time-range queries. Random IDs (v4) scatter inserts → poor locality. This is v7 value over fully random v4.

tradeoff: v7 的排序性与隐私优势 vs v1 的历史兼容性
optionExplanations: v7 和 v1 编码长度基本一样，长度从来不是它被推荐的原因。
v1 同样带毫秒级时间戳，精度从来不是问题所在。
时间戳前置带来字符串可排序，加上不含 MAC 地址避免隐私泄露，这两点才是真正被推荐的理由。
v7 是 RFC 9562 定义的公开标准，任何系统都能生成，跟 AWS 或 DynamoDB 没关系。
optionExplanations_en: v7 and v1 encode to roughly the same length -- length was never why it's recommended.
v1 also carries a millisecond timestamp, so precision was never the real issue.
Putting the timestamp first makes the string sortable, and dropping the MAC address avoids the privacy leak -- those are the two real reasons to prefer it.
v7 is defined in the public RFC 9562 standard, generatable by any system -- it has nothing to do with AWS.
scenario: 面向公网的订单表要选 ID 方案，既要按时间排序，又不能泄露生成机器的信息。
scenario_en: For a public-facing orders table you need IDs that sort by time and leak nothing about the machine that minted them.

q: 现代 DynamoDB 的分区定位机制与 2007 年 Dynamo 论文的区别是？
q_en: How does modern DynamoDB's partition-location mechanism differ from the 2007 Dynamo paper?
options: 现代 DynamoDB 用点对点哈希环，和论文一致
论文用中心化服务，现代版反而改用 gossip 协议

options_en: An index with the same partition key as the base table, only a different sort key.

An index that can only be created at table creation and never added later.
An inverted index for full-text search across the whole table.

q: LSI（本地二级索引）的定义是？
q_en: What is the definition of an LSI (Local Secondary Index)?
options: 分区键与主表不同的独立索引，单独分区
跨 AWS region 复制的只读索引副本
分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区
表在某个时间点的只读快照备份
why: LSI 保持同一个分区键、换一个排序维度，物理上与主表 item 放在相同分区里，在每个分区内维护一棵按 LSI 排序键索引的独立 B-tree。
why_en: A local secondary index keeps the table's partition key but uses a different sort key and is co-located on the same physical partitions.
options_en: A standalone index whose partition key differs from the base table's, with its own partitions.
A read-only index replica copied across AWS regions.
Same partition key as the base table, a different sort key, colocated in the same partition.
A read-only snapshot backup of the table at a point in time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。

分区键不变、只换排序维度，物理上和主表 item 挤在同一个分区里，随主表写同步更新。
LSI 是实时同步的索引，不是某个时间点的静态快照。
optionExplanations_en: Changing the partition key is GSI's definition, misapplied to LSI here.
Cross-region replication is Global Tables' job, entirely separate from LSI.
The partition key stays the same and only the sort dimension changes, physically co-located with the base table's items and updated synchronously with it.
An LSI stays live and current, not a static snapshot frozen at a point in time.

options: AP：可用性优先，可能读到旧数据
CP：一致性优先，分区时牺牲可用性
同时保证 C、A、P 三者
CA：不容忍网络分区的单机式系统
why: 默认最终一致时 DynamoDB 表现为 AP/BASE：读可以由任意副本服务，可能略陈旧；需要时再按请求切强一致。
why_en: With default eventual consistency DynamoDB generally behaves as an available AP system with BASE properties.
options_en: AP: availability first, so a read may return stale data.
CP: consistency first, giving up availability during a partition.
It guarantees C, A, and P all at the same time.
CA: a single-machine style system that tolerates no network partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统三选二权衡：一致性、可用性、分区容错性最多同时保证两项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can only fully guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 里选择可用性和分区容错、牺牲强一致性的系统类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AP system prioritizes availability and partition tolerance over strong consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 与 ACID 相对的宽松一致性模型：基本可用、软状态、最终一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BASE is a looser consistency model: basically available, soft state, and eventually consistent.
termDefinitions.fullName: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent

optionExplanations: 默认最终一致时读可以打到任意副本、延迟低，代价是可能读到略旧的数据，这正是 AP 的取舍。
如果真是 CP，分区发生时读请求会被拒绝以保一致性，这跟「默认优先可用」的行为正相反。
这违反了 CAP 定理本身——三者不可能被同时完全保证。
分布式系统跑在多台机器和多个 AZ 上，网络分区是必须容忍的常态，不能假装不会发生。
optionExplanations_en: Under default eventual consistency, reads can hit any replica for low latency, at the cost of possibly returning slightly stale data -- that's the AP tradeoff.
If it were truly CP, reads would be rejected during a partition to preserve consistency -- the opposite of the default availability-first behavior.
This violates the CAP theorem itself -- all three can never be fully guaranteed at once.
Running across many machines and Availability Zones, a distributed system has to treat network partitions as a given, not assume they won't happen.
scenario: 跨可用区部署的商品页读接口，用 DynamoDB 默认读模式承接全部流量。
scenario_en: A product-page read endpoint spans availability zones and serves all traffic with DynamoDB default reads.

q: 强一致读比最终一致读贵多少？
q_en: How much more expensive is a strongly consistent read than an eventually consistent one?
options: 两者定价完全一样
要贵上整整 10 倍
按 4KB 读计费，贵一倍。
反而比强一致读的价格还要便宜整整一半
why: 强一致读消耗双倍读容量（1 vs 0.5 RCU per 4KB）并可能略慢，换来「读一定反映此前所有成功写入」的保证。
why_en: A strongly consistent read costs one RCU per four kilobytes, twice the half RCU of an eventually consistent read.
options_en: The two are priced exactly the same.
It costs a full ten times as much.
It is twice as much when billed per 4KB read.
It is actually half the price of a strongly consistent read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读容量单位：一个 RCU 每秒最多读 4KB（强一致 1 次或最终一致 2 次）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读请求里的参数，设为 true 即要求强一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ConsistentRead is a per-request parameter that, when set to true, requires a strongly consistent read.

scenario: 一个下单确认页要求强一致读，团队想知道这比默认的最终一致读贵多少。
scenario_en: An order-confirmation page requires a strongly consistent read, and the team wants to know how much pricier that is than the default eventually consistent read.
optionExplanations: 两者的计费单价其实不同，不存在完全一样这回事。
10 倍是编造的倍数，实际差距远没有这么夸张。
强一致读每 4KB 算 1 RCU，最终一致读只算 0.5 RCU，正好是两倍关系。
这把贵和便宜的方向说反了，强一致读只会更贵不会更便宜。
optionExplanations_en: The two are actually billed at different per-unit rates -- they're not identical.
Ten times is a fabricated multiplier -- the real gap is nowhere near that large.
A strong read costs 1 RCU per 4KB versus 0.5 RCU for eventual -- exactly double.
This reverses the direction -- strong consistency only ever costs more, never less.

q: DynamoDB 的 ACID 事务支持范围是？
q_en: What's the scope of DynamoDB's ACID transaction support?
options: 完全不支持任何形式的事务
只支持单个 item 内的事务
只支持单表内的多 item 事务
支持跨表事务，最多 100 item
why: DynamoDB 事务支持跨表、最多 100 个 item、可串行化隔离——预订类等需要原子多项写的场景可以直接用。
why_en: Transact write and get items provide serializable ACID transactions across up to one hundred items spanning multiple tables.
options_en: It supports no form of transaction at all.
It only supports transactions within a single item.
It only supports multi-item transactions inside one table.
It supports cross-table transactions, up to 100 items each.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库事务的四个安全属性：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID describes the four safety guarantees a transaction provides: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的多项原子写入 API，跨表提供可串行化隔离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TransactWriteItems is DynamoDB's API for committing multiple writes atomically across tables with serializable isolation.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的多项原子读取 API，在一次事务里读取多个 item。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TransactGetItems reads multiple items together as a single atomic transaction.

scenario: 设计一个需要跨表原子写入的下单流程。
scenario_en: Designing a checkout flow that needs an atomic write across multiple tables.
optionExplanations: 这是过时的老批评，TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems 早就把这个短板补上了。
低估了范围，一个事务能打包最多 100 个 item，不止一条。
低估了范围，事务能跨越多张表一起提交，不局限于单表。
能跨表提交、单次上限 100 条、隔离级别可串行化，预订下单这类需要原子多项写的场景可以直接用，不用自己写补偿逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: This is the old, outdated criticism -- TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems closed that gap long ago.
This undersells it -- a single transaction can bundle up to 100 items, not just one.
This undersells it -- a transaction can commit across multiple tables at once, not just one.
Cross-table, up to 100 items, serializable isolation -- booking or checkout flows needing atomic multi-item writes can use this directly, no compensation logic needed.

q: 设计需要强一致读的访问模式时，必须注意哪个索引限制？
q_en: When designing an access pattern that needs strongly consistent reads, which index limitation must you keep in mind?
options: LSI 不支持强一致读
只有主表和 LSI 支持强一致。
主表不支持强一致读
强一致读其实反而只有走 GSI 才能支持
why: GSI 异步维护、注定最终一致；若某访问模式要求强一致，就必须让它落在主表或 LSI 上，不能设计成走 GSI。
why_en: Strongly consistent reads work only on the base table and LSIs, never on GSIs, which constrains access-pattern design.
options_en: LSI does not support strongly consistent reads.
Only the base table and LSIs support strong consistency.
The base table does not support strongly consistent reads.
Strong consistency is somehow only available by going through a GSI.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引：分区键与主表不同，独立物理分区，只支持最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Global Secondary Index has its own partition key and its own physical partitions, and it only supports eventually consistent reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Local Secondary Index shares the table's partition key but uses a different sort key, and is co-located with the base table.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读请求里的参数，设为 true 即要求强一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ConsistentRead is a per-request parameter that, when set to true, requires a strongly consistent read.

optionExplanations: LSI 与主表同步更新、同分区共存，其实和主表一样支持强一致读。
GSI 靠异步方式维护索引，天生只能最终一致；需要强一致的访问模式只能落在主表或 LSI，绕不开这条限制。
主表恰恰是强一致读的默认可用位置，这个说法正好说反了。
方向完全说反了，GSI 才是唯一不支持强一致读的那个。
optionExplanations_en: An LSI updates synchronously and co-locates with the base table, so it actually supports strong consistency just like the base table does.
A GSI is asynchronously maintained and destined to be eventual-only; any access pattern needing strong consistency must land on the base table or an LSI, never a GSI.
The base table is exactly where strong consistency is available by default -- this has it backwards.
This is completely reversed -- a GSI is in fact the one index that never supports strong consistency.
scenario: 支付回调后要立刻按订单号读到最新状态，而这条查询目前走的是二级索引。
scenario_en: Right after a payment callback you must read the newest order status, and that query goes through a secondary index.

q: 最终一致读在底层是如何服务的？为什么可能读到旧数据？
q_en: How is an eventually consistent read served under the hood, and why might it return stale data?
options: 永远由 leader 主副本服务，所以绝不会读到旧数据
从磁盘快照读取
任意副本可服务，follower 可能滞后。
由客户端缓存服务
why: 最终一致读可以打到任意副本（低延迟、省容量），但 follower 的数据是 leader 异步推的，可能落后一拍——这就是「可能读不到最新写」的来源。
why_en: Eventually consistent reads can be served by any of the three replicas, and followers may lag because the leader replicates asynchronously.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Client read"] --> R1["replica A"]
    C --> R2["replica B"]
    R1 --> Old["may be stale"]
    R2 --> New["may be newer"]
options_en: It is always served by the leader replica, so it can never be stale.
It reads from a disk snapshot.
Any replica can serve it, and a follower may lag.
It is served by a client-side cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 达成确认所需的最小副本数，这里是 3 副本中的 2 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas -- here two out of three -- that must acknowledge a write.

optionExplanations: 只由 leader 服务是强一致读的行为，最终一致读为了低延迟反而会打到任意副本。
没有磁盘快照这回事，读的是副本当下的实时数据。
为了低延迟，最终一致读可以打到任意副本，而副本上的数据是从 leader 异步同步过来的，落后一拍就会读到旧值。
DAX 才是可选的额外缓存层，不是最终一致读的默认实现方式。
optionExplanations_en: Being served only by the leader is strong-read behavior; eventual reads hit any replica precisely for lower latency.
There's no disk snapshot involved -- it reads a replica's current live data.
For lower latency, eventual reads can hit any replica, and since followers get data pushed asynchronously from the leader, a lagging one can return a stale value.
DAX is the optional extra caching layer, not the default mechanism behind eventual reads.
scenario: 刚写完的用户资料马上用默认读模式读回来，偶尔拿到的还是旧值。
scenario_en: You write a user profile and immediately read it back with default reads, and sometimes still get the old value.

q: 强一致读在底层是如何保证「一定最新」的？
q_en: How does a strongly consistent read guarantee it's always current under the hood?
options: 直接路由到 leader 读取
同时读取全部三个副本再取多数派的值
读之前先触发一次全量同步
读前锁住整个分区阻塞写入
why: 强一致读绕过 follower、直达 leader；因为写路径全部经过 leader，读它就等于读到所有已成功的写。代价是更高的容量消耗和可能略高的延迟。
why_en: Strongly consistent reads route directly to the partition leader, which sees every write first and therefore always has the latest data.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Strong read"] --> Leader["leader or quorum path"]
    Leader --> Check["confirm latest write"]
    Check --> Item["return newest item"]
options_en: It routes the read straight to the leader.
It reads all three replicas at once and takes the majority value.
It triggers a full sync before the read.
It locks the whole partition and blocks writes before reading.
optionExplanations: 所有写入都要先落到 leader，强一致读绕开 follower 直接找它要数据，自然能看到全部已确认的写，代价是更高的容量消耗。
DynamoDB 的强一致读不做多数派投票，那是另一类系统的方案。
每次读都全量同步会让延迟暴涨，跟单毫秒级响应完全不符。
锁住整个分区会严重拖累并发写入，跟实际「代价只是双倍 RCU」完全不符。
optionExplanations_en: Every write goes through the leader, so a strong read bypasses followers and goes straight to it -- it naturally sees every successful write, at the cost of higher capacity use.
DynamoDB's strong reads don't take a majority vote -- that belongs to a different class of system.
Fully resyncing on every read would blow up latency, incompatible with single-digit-millisecond response times.
Locking the whole partition would badly hurt concurrent writes, nothing like the real cost of just double the RCUs.
scenario: 账户余额扣减后必须立刻读到最新值，接口因此设了 ConsistentRead=true。
scenario_en: After debiting a balance you must read the newest value, so the call sets ConsistentRead=true.

q: DynamoDB 如何自动扩展分区？
q_en: How does DynamoDB automatically scale partitions?
options: 需要手动提交工单向 AWS 申请扩容
到容量上限自动拆分重分布。
只能整表重建来扩容
分区永远固定不变
why: auto-sharding：分区在大小或吞吐到顶时自动 split，配合哈希分区的均匀分布实现无停机水平扩展——这是「全托管」的核心体现。
why_en: When a partition hits its size or throughput limit DynamoDB automatically splits it and redistributes data with hash partitioning keeping load even.
options_en: You must manually file a ticket to AWS to request capacity expansion.
Automatically splits and redistributes once capacity is hit.
The only way to scale is to rebuild the entire table.
Partitions are permanently fixed and never change.
scenario: 表的数据量和流量都在持续增长。
scenario_en: A table's data volume and traffic keep growing.
optionExplanations: 全托管的意义正是要消灭这种人工审批工单，扩容不需要人介入。
分区大小或吞吐一到上限就自动拆分重分布，配合哈希分区均匀分布，全程无停机。
整表重建意味着停机和大规模数据迁移，跟实际的无停机扩展完全不符。
分区固定不变会让表数据增长后彻底扩不动，跟「高可扩展」的定位正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Being fully managed exists precisely to eliminate this kind of manual approval ticket -- scaling needs no human in the loop.
Once a partition hits its size or throughput ceiling it auto-splits and redistributes, staying evenly balanced via hash partitioning, all without downtime.
A full table rebuild means downtime and mass data migration, nothing like real zero-downtime scaling.
Fixed, unchanging partitions would leave a table unable to grow at all, the opposite of the 'highly scalable' positioning.

scenario: 面试中设计一个全球化应用，用户分布在北美、欧洲、亚洲三地。
scenario_en: In an interview you design a global application whose users sit in North America, Europe, and Asia.
q: 要让各大洲用户都低延迟读写，应该点名 DynamoDB 的哪个特性？
q_en: To give users on every continent low-latency reads and writes, which DynamoDB feature do you name?
options: 给每个用户建一张表
把所有读写流量都固定路由到 us-east-1
在客户端做全部缓存
Global Tables 跨区域实时复制。
why: Global Tables 跨区域实时复制，各地用户就近读写。计量单位是 region 数：N 个 region ≈ 每次写计 N 份复制写容量，延迟换成本。
why_en: Global Tables replicate in real time across regions so users read and write locally; the unit you count is regions -- with N regions each write costs N replicated write units, so you trade cost for latency.
whenOtherWins: 单区域应用不需要 Global Tables，区域内的多 AZ 冗余已经保证了高可用。
options_en: Create a separate table for every user.
Permanently route all read and write traffic to us-east-1.
Cache everything entirely on the client.
Global Tables replicate in real time across regions.
tradeoff: 跨区域就近读写 vs 单区域集中但跨洲延迟高

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的跨区域复制功能，让各地用户就近读写同一份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Global Tables replicate a DynamoDB table across regions so users everywhere can read and write nearby.

optionExplanations: 按用户分表跟跨区域延迟毫无关系，还会造出海量表的管理噩梦。
所有流量打到单个 region 意味着其他大洲用户依旧要背负跨洲往返延迟，问题根本没解决。
写入和多端同步终究要经过后端，客户端缓存帮不上跨洲延迟的忙。
只需在控制台勾选目标 region，这项功能就能把数据跨区域实时复制，让各地用户就近读写。
optionExplanations_en: Per-user tables have nothing to do with cross-region latency and create a table-management nightmare.
Routing everything to one region still leaves users on other continents paying the cross-continent round trip -- the problem isn't solved.
Writes and cross-device sync still have to hit the backend eventually, so client-side caching doesn't touch cross-continent latency.
Just check off the target regions in the console, and Global Tables replicates in real time so users everywhere read and write nearby.

q: DynamoDB 在单个 region 内的复制拓扑是？
q_en: What is DynamoDB's replication topology within a single region?
options: 两副本，用户可配置
自动跨 3 AZ 复制，3 副本不可配置。
单副本，靠备份兜底
副本数随流量动态在 1-10 之间变化
why: 三 AZ、三副本（1 leader + 2 follower）是固定设计，不给用户配置项；跨区域冗余才需要额外开 Global Tables。
why_en: DynamoDB automatically keeps three replicas across three availability zones per partition, one leader and two followers, with no user configuration.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    P["Logical partition"] --> AZ1["replica AZ1"]
    P --> AZ2["replica AZ2"]
    P --> AZ3["replica AZ3"]
    AZ1 --> Q["quorum writes"]
    AZ2 --> Q
    AZ3 --> Q
options_en: Two replicas, user-configurable.
Automatically replicated across three AZs with three fixed, non-configurable replicas.
A single replica backed by periodic backups.
Replica count scales dynamically between one and ten based on traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 数据中心的独立故障域；DynamoDB 默认跨 3 个 AZ 复制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Availability Zone is an independent failure domain in AWS, and DynamoDB replicates across three of them by default.

scenario: 评估 DynamoDB 默认的容灾能力是否够用。
scenario_en: Evaluating whether DynamoDB's default disaster-recovery posture is good enough.
optionExplanations: 副本数和 AZ 分布是固定设计，不存在给用户配置的入口。
三个 AZ、三副本是固定不变的默认设计，这是硬件故障或网络中断下仍保持可用的基础。
单副本加备份意味着实时故障切换能力弱得多，跟实际的默认冗余完全不符。
副本数不会随流量变化，流量增长靠分区拆分应对，不是靠增减副本。
optionExplanations_en: Replica count and AZ distribution are a fixed design -- there's no configuration surface for this.
Three AZs and three replicas are the fixed default, and that's what keeps it available through a hardware failure or network outage.
Single-replica-plus-backup implies far weaker real-time failover than the actual default redundancy.
Replica count never tracks traffic -- growth is handled by partition splitting, not by adding or removing replicas.

q: 把 DynamoDB 分区写入的底层流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the underlying steps of a DynamoDB partition write in the correct order:
steps: 写请求路由到该分区的 leader 节点
quorum（3 个中的 2 个）持久化日志记录后，写入即确认成功
leader 生成 WAL（写前日志）条目
leader 把日志条目发送给复制组的 peer 节点
why: 每个分区是一个基于 Multi-Paxos 的 3 节点 leader 复制组：leader 写 WAL → 发给 peers → 2/3 quorum 持久化即 ack。这解释了强一致读为什么找 leader。
why_en: The partition leader writes a WAL entry, sends it to its peers, and acknowledges the write once a quorum of two out of three persists it.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant L as Leader
    participant F1 as Follower1
    participant F2 as Follower2
    C->>L: 写请求
    L->>L: 生成 WAL 条目
    L->>F1: 发送日志
    L->>F2: 发送日志
    F1-->>L: 已持久化
    Note over L: quorum 2/3 达成
    L-->>C: 确认写入

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志：写入先落日志再应用，保证持久性和可恢复性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records a write before it is applied, guaranteeing durability and recoverability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 达成确认所需的最小副本数，这里是 3 副本中的 2 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas -- here two out of three -- that must acknowledge a write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持连续多轮决议的 Paxos 共识协议变体，靠稳定 leader 做日志复制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-Paxos is a consensus protocol variant that agrees on a sequence of log entries via a stable leader.

q: 公开资料中，DynamoDB 每个分区复制组通常可以怎么理解？
q_en: Based on public information, how can DynamoDB's per-partition replication group generally be described?
options: Gossip 协议，节点间对等传播
两阶段提交，由跨节点的中央协调者收集并统计各方投票
leader 复制组，quorum 持久化
无协议，各副本异步尽力复制
why: 更稳妥的面试说法是：分区由 leader-based 复制组服务，写入经过日志和 quorum 持久化后确认。AWS 论文提到过相关共识实现，但 DynamoDB 是闭源服务，别把某个协议名当作永远不变的 API 语义。
why_en: Since DynamoDB is closed source, the safer answer is a leader-based replication group with quorum-backed writes, not a specific protocol name.
options_en: A gossip protocol propagating state peer to peer.
Two-phase commit with a central coordinator collecting and tallying votes across nodes.
A leader-based replica group with quorum-durable writes.
No protocol -- replicas just copy asynchronously, best effort.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点间随机两两交换信息、最终扩散到全网的去中心化协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gossip protocol lets nodes spread state by randomly exchanging information pairwise until it reaches the whole cluster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 达成确认所需的最小副本数，这里是 3 副本中的 2 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas -- here two out of three -- that must acknowledge a write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分两阶段（准备+提交）让多个参与方达成一致的协议，常用于跨库事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit coordinates multiple participants to agree via a prepare phase and a commit phase, often used for cross-database transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 每个分区的数据复制在 3 个节点(跨 3 AZ)上,组成一个「leader 复制组」:1 leader + 2 follower。写→leader 写 WAL→发给 follower→多数(2/3)持久化即 ack(quorum);强一致读走 leader、最终一致读走任意副本。底层是 Multi-Paxos 类共识,但 DynamoDB 闭源,面试稳妥说法=「leader 复制组 + quorum 持久化」,别把某个协议名当死语义
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Each DynamoDB partition is replicated on 3 nodes across 3 AZs as a leader-based replication group: 1 leader + 2 followers. Write → leader writes WAL → sends to followers → acked once a quorum (2/3) persist; strong reads go to the leader, eventual reads to any replica. It uses Multi-Paxos-style consensus, but DynamoDB is closed-source, so the safe interview phrasing is a leader-based replication group with quorum durability.

scenario: 被追问 DynamoDB 分区内部到底靠什么协议做复制。
scenario_en: Getting pressed on exactly what protocol DynamoDB's partitions use internally for replication.
optionExplanations: Gossip 更贴近去中心化的成员发现和状态传播，不是描述单个分区内的复制机制。
两阶段提交协调的是跨节点/跨库的多方一致，不是单个分区内部的日志复制。
更稳妥的说法是分区由带 leader 的复制组服务，写入要经过日志和多数派确认才算落盘——它闭源，别把某个协议名当成一成不变的事实。
没有 quorum 确认，写入的持久性和一致性都没法保证，这跟它宣称的可靠性不符。
optionExplanations_en: Gossip fits decentralized membership discovery and state propagation, not the replication mechanism inside one partition.
Two-phase commit coordinates agreement across separate nodes or databases, not log replication within a single partition.

The safer description is a leader-based replica group whose writes are durable once the log and quorum confirm -- DynamoDB is closed source, so no protocol name should be treated as a fixed guarantee.
Without a quorum acknowledgment, neither durability nor consistency of the write could be guaranteed, which doesn't match its reliability claims.

q: 关于 DynamoDB 的加密，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about DynamoDB's encryption is correct?
options: 需要手动开启静态加密
静态加密默认开启，TLS 强制传输。
只加密传输途中的数据，落盘存储时并不加密
加密需要额外付费开通
why: 静态加密和传输加密是两件事：数据写入持久存储前默认已加密；TLS 则保护到 DynamoDB API 路上的请求和响应。
why_en: Split it into two layers: encryption at rest is on by default before data reaches durable storage, and TLS protects requests and responses on the way to the DynamoDB API.
options_en: You must manually enable encryption at rest.
Encryption at rest is on by default and TLS is enforced in transit.
Only data in transit is encrypted; data at rest on disk is not.
Encryption requires an extra paid add-on.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTPS 底层的传输加密协议:在客户端和 DynamoDB API 之间建加密通道,防请求/响应在网络上被窃听或篡改
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS (Transport Layer Security) is the transport encryption under HTTPS: it builds an encrypted channel between the client and the DynamoDB API so requests/responses cannot be sniffed or tampered with in transit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 静态加密:数据落盘存储时被加密。DynamoDB 从建表起默认开、不能关、不额外收费,底层用信封加密+KMS。防的是「磁盘/备份被拿走」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encryption at rest: data is encrypted when stored on disk. DynamoDB has it on by default from table creation, cannot disable, no extra cost, using envelope encryption + KMS. Protects against stolen disks/backups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输加密:数据在网络上传输时被加密,靠 TLS。DynamoDB API 强制 HTTPS。防的是「网络路上被窃听/篡改」。和静态加密是两个阶段:一个存着时、一个传输时
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encryption in transit: data is encrypted while moving over the network, via TLS. The DynamoDB API is HTTPS-only. Protects against eavesdropping/tampering on the wire — a different stage from at-rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 信封加密(密钥分两层):①用一把「数据密钥(DEK)」加密真正的数据 ②再用「主密钥(在 KMS 里)」把这把数据密钥加密(=「装进信封」)③加密后的数据密钥跟数据存一起。好处:主密钥永不离开 KMS;轮换主密钥只需重新加密那些小小的数据密钥、不用重加密全部数据;数据密钥做大批量对称加密(快)、主密钥只封套
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Envelope encryption (two key layers): (1) a data key (DEK) encrypts the actual data; (2) a master key (in KMS) encrypts that data key ("wrapped in an envelope"); (3) the encrypted data key is stored with the data. Benefits: the master key never leaves KMS; rotating it only re-encrypts the small data keys, not all data; the data key does fast bulk symmetric encryption.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真正用来加密数据的那把密钥。它本身以「被主密钥加密后」的形态存着(信封加密);读数据时先用 KMS 里的主密钥把它解开,再用它解数据
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The data key (DEK) is the key that actually encrypts the data. It is stored in encrypted form (wrapped by the master key); to read, the master key in KMS unwraps it, then it decrypts the data.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  App["应用/服务"] -->|"TLS / HTTPS\n传输中加密"| API["DynamoDB API"]
  API -->|"服务端静态加密\n写入前加密"| Store["密文数据\n表 / 索引 / 备份"]
  KMS["KMS / wrapping key"] -->|"加密 data key"| DK["encrypted data key"]
  DK -.-> Store
scenario: 系统里存有用户的敏感信息。
scenario_en: The system stores sensitive user information.
optionExplanations: 静态加密其实从建表起就默认打开，不需要用户手动做任何配置。
落盘前默认做静态加密，加上 API 路上强制走 TLS，两层保护同时覆盖存储和传输。
这只说对了一半，静态加密同样是默认行为，不是只加密传输。
两层加密都不额外收费，是服务默认自带的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Encryption at rest is actually on by default from the moment the table is created -- no manual setup required.
Data is encrypted by default before it's written to storage, and TLS is enforced for every API call, covering both storage and transit.
This only gets half right -- encryption at rest is equally the default, not just transit.
Neither layer costs extra -- both come included with the service by default.

q: DynamoDB 提供哪些访问控制/网络安全手段？（多选）
q_en: Which access-control/network-security mechanisms does DynamoDB provide? (select all)
options: IAM 集成：细粒度策略控制谁能访问、能做什么操作
VPC endpoint：从 VPC 内安全访问，不暴露到公网
静态数据默认加密
内置用户名密码表
why: 访问控制走 IAM 策略，网络隔离走 VPC endpoint，存储安全靠默认加密；DynamoDB 没有自己的用户名密码体系。
why_en: Access control comes from IAM policies, network isolation from VPC endpoints, and storage safety from default encryption at rest.
options_en: IAM integration: fine-grained policies control who can access what and which actions they can perform.
VPC endpoints: access securely from within a VPC without exposing traffic to the public internet.
Data at rest is encrypted by default.
A built-in username/password table.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的身份与权限管理服务，用策略控制谁能访问哪些资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IAM is AWS's identity and access management service, controlling who can access which resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 内的隔离虚拟网络；VPC endpoint 让流量不经公网访问服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A VPC is an isolated virtual network in AWS, and a VPC endpoint reaches a service without crossing the public internet.

optionExplanations: 谁能访问、能做什么操作，全靠 IAM 策略挡住越权请求，而不是数据库自带的权限系统。
请求路径完全留在 AWS 内网，VPC endpoint 挡住了暴露到公网的风险，不用额外配防火墙规则。
静态数据默认加密兜底存储安全，不需要额外配置就能挡住裸盘泄露的风险。
身份认证统一交给 IAM，DynamoDB 本身不维护账号密码这类东西。
optionExplanations_en: Who can access what and do what is entirely gated by IAM policies, not a database-native permission system.
The request path stays entirely inside AWS's network -- a VPC endpoint blocks public-internet exposure with no extra firewall rules needed.
Default encryption at rest backstops storage security, blocking raw-disk leakage with no extra configuration.
Identity authentication is delegated entirely to IAM -- DynamoDB itself keeps no accounts or passwords.
scenario: 把 DynamoDB 接进有合规要求的内网服务：流量不能走公网，权限要按角色细分。
scenario_en: You wire DynamoDB into a compliance-bound internal service: no public-internet traffic, role-scoped permissions.

scenario: 两个业务：A 流量高度不可预测、忽高忽低；B 流量稳定可预测、长期在线。分别选 DynamoDB 计费模式。
scenario_en: Two workloads: A has highly unpredictable, spiky traffic; B has steady, predictable, always-on traffic. Choose a DynamoDB billing mode for each.
q: 正确的搭配是？
q_en: What's the right pairing?
options: A 用 on-demand，B 用 provisioned。
都用 on-demand
A 用 provisioned；B 用 on-demand
都用 provisioned
why: on-demand 按请求计费，适合不可预测的负载；provisioned 预先指定 RCU/WCU 按小时计费，可预测负载下更省，但低谷期会有闲置容量。
why_en: On-demand per-request pricing suits unpredictable workloads while provisioned capacity is more cost-effective for predictable steady traffic.
whenOtherWins: 稳定负载硬用 on-demand 会明显更贵；波动负载用 provisioned 则要么限流要么大量闲置。
options_en: A uses on-demand, B uses provisioned capacity.
Both use on-demand.
A uses provisioned; B uses on-demand.
Both use provisioned capacity.
tradeoff: 按请求付费应对波动 vs 预置容量应对稳定负载

termDefinitions.meaning: 按实际请求量计费的容量模式，适合不可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-demand capacity bills per request, which suits unpredictable traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先指定读写容量单位、按小时计费的模式，适合稳定可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Provisioned capacity bills hourly for pre-specified read and write units, which suits steady, predictable traffic.

optionExplanations: A 波动就按请求付费，避免为峰值预留浪费；B 稳定就用预置容量，按小时计费更省钱。
稳定负载 B 硬用 on-demand 会持续按请求单价付费，比预置容量明显更贵。
把两种负载和计费模式的搭配整个对调了，波动负载用 provisioned 要么限流要么闲置，两头都不划算。
波动负载 A 硬用 provisioned，遇到尖峰会限流、遇到低谷又浪费闲置容量。
optionExplanations_en: A is bursty, so pay-per-request avoids over-provisioning for peaks; B is steady, so hourly provisioned capacity is cheaper.
Forcing steady-load B onto on-demand keeps paying the per-request premium continuously, clearly costlier than provisioned.
This swaps the two workload-to-mode pairings entirely -- provisioned under bursty load throttles or sits idle either way.
Forcing bursty A onto provisioned capacity means throttling at peaks and wasted idle capacity in the quiet periods.

q: 补全容量单位的定义：
q_en: Fill in the definitions of the capacity units:
text: 1 个 RCU = 每秒读取最多 {{4KB}} 数据（强一致 1 次 / 最终一致 2 次）；1 个 WCU = 每秒写入最多 {{1KB}} 数据。
why: RCU 以 4KB 为读取单位、WCU 以 1KB 为写入单位；同一个 RCU 能换 2 次最终一致读，这是最终一致省一半钱的由来。
why_en: One read capacity unit covers four kilobytes per second and one write capacity unit covers one kilobyte per second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读容量单位：一个 RCU 每秒最多读 4KB（强一致 1 次或最终一致 2 次）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

scenario: 在预估某张表的读写成本之前，需要先搞清楚 RCU 和 WCU 各自的计量单位。
scenario_en: Before estimating a table's read/write cost, you first need to know what RCU and WCU each measure.

q: DynamoDB 底层会怎么应对这个写入需求？
q_en: How will DynamoDB handle this write load under the hood?
options: 自动把数据横向拆分到足够多的分区，让总吞吐超过单分区上限
让单个分区独自扛下全部吞吐，靠换用更快的 SSD 磁盘硬顶住上限
必须手工申请分区扩容工单，AWS 才会拆分
自动把访问模式降级为最终一致读来省吞吐
why: 单分区上限约 3,000 RCU / 1,000 WCU；超过时 DynamoDB 靠 auto-sharding 自动拆分并重新分布数据，这是估算需要多少分区的依据。
why_en: A single partition caps out around three thousand RCUs and one thousand WCUs, so DynamoDB automatically splits data across more partitions once demand exceeds that limit.
scenario: 一张表预计需要持续 5,000 WCU 的写入吞吐（已知单分区写入上限约 1,000 WCU）。
scenario_en: A table needs to sustain 5,000 WCU of write throughput (given that a single partition caps out around 1,000 WCU).
options_en: Automatically split the data horizontally across enough partitions so total throughput exceeds the single-partition cap.
Let a single partition absorb all the throughput by swapping in faster SSD disks.
Require a manual capacity-expansion ticket before AWS will split the partition.
Automatically downgrade reads to eventual consistency to save throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读容量单位：一个 RCU 每秒最多读 4KB（强一致 1 次或最终一致 2 次）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

optionExplanations: 单分区吞吐撞到约 1,000 WCU 的天花板后，系统会自动把数据横向拆到更多分区并重新分布，让总吞吐突破这个限制。
单分区的读写上限是固定的，不管磁盘多快都顶不住持续超限的吞吐。
全托管的意义就是消灭这种人工工单，拆分是自动完成的，不需要申请。
降级一致性等级不会改变写入吞吐上限，跟这个写入需求的问题完全不相关。
optionExplanations_en: Once a single partition's throughput hits its roughly 1,000 WCU ceiling, auto-sharding automatically splits and redistributes data, pushing total throughput past that per-partition limit.
A single partition's read/write ceiling is fixed -- no disk speed can sustain throughput past it indefinitely.
Being fully managed exists to eliminate this kind of manual ticket -- splitting happens automatically, no request needed.
Downgrading consistency does nothing to raise the write-throughput ceiling -- it's unrelated to this write demand.

q: 用 DynamoDB 记 YouTube 播放数，每次写只有几十字节，为什么每次写仍消耗 1 个完整 WCU？
q_en: Storing YouTube view counts in DynamoDB, each write is only a few dozen bytes -- why does every write still cost one full WCU?
options: 因为播放数是数字类型，计费更贵
WCU 向上取整到 1KB
因为每次写要复制三份副本
因为表上没有开启压缩选项
why: WCU 向上取整到 1KB：小写照样吃满 1 WCU，于是单分区约 1,000 写/秒。若要 1,000 万写/秒就需要约 1 万个分区——这个约束直接影响架构。
why_en: Every write consumes at least one WCU because DynamoDB rounds up to the nearest kilobyte, capping a partition at about a thousand writes per second.
options_en: Because the play count is a numeric type, which bills higher.
A WCU rounds up to 1KB.
Because every write is replicated to three copies.
Because compression is not enabled on the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

scenario: 在 DynamoDB 里记录一个高频但单条数据很小的计数器，比如播放数。
scenario_en: Recording a high-frequency but tiny counter in DynamoDB, such as a view count.
optionExplanations: 属性是数字、字符串还是布尔类型都不影响计费，跟数据类型没关系。
WCU 按字节大小向上取整到 1KB，哪怕只写几十字节也要吃满整整 1 个 WCU。
三副本复制是持久性机制，用户按逻辑写入次数付费，不会因副本数变化。
计费单位就是字节大小向上取整，压缩不是计费维度，开不开都一样。
optionExplanations_en: Billing looks only at byte size, not whether the attribute is a number, string, or boolean.
A WCU rounds byte size up to the nearest kilobyte, so even a write of a few dozen bytes still consumes a full WCU.
Three-way replication is a durability mechanism -- users pay per logical write, not per replica.
The billing unit is simply byte size rounded up; compression isn't a billing dimension either way.

q: 假设 1,000 万写/秒的负载跑在 DynamoDB 上（预置容量约 $0.00065/WCU-小时），日成本量级大约是？
q_en: Assuming a load of ten million writes per second on DynamoDB (provisioned pricing around $0.00065 per WCU-hour), roughly what order of magnitude is the daily cost?
options: 约 $150 一天，几乎可以忽略
约 $1,500 一天，属于小额开销
约 $15.6 万一天
落在免费额度内，无需付费
why: 这笔账的意义在于「gut check」：超高写入量在 DynamoDB 上成本可能高到不现实，这正是「成本效率」成为不选它的理由之一。
why_en: Ten million writes per second costs roughly one hundred fifty six thousand dollars a day on provisioned capacity, a sanity check on feasibility.
options_en: About $150 a day -- basically negligible.
About $1,500 a day -- a small line item.
About $156,000 a day.
It falls inside the free tier, so nothing to pay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先指定读写容量单位、按小时计费的模式，适合稳定可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Provisioned capacity bills hourly for pre-specified read and write units, which suits steady, predictable traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按实际请求量计费的容量模式，适合不可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-demand capacity bills per request, which suits unpredictable traffic.

scenario: 团队评估把 YouTube 播放量写入 DynamoDB 是否现实，负载假设为 1,000 万写/秒。
scenario_en: The team is evaluating whether writing YouTube view counts into DynamoDB is realistic, assuming a load of ten million writes per second.
optionExplanations: 这个量级低了三个数量级，跟 1,000 万写/秒的规模完全对不上。
这个量级还是低了两个数量级，撑不起千万级写入的真实账单。
1,000 万 WCU × $0.00065/小时 × 24 小时，算下来是十万美元量级，这笔账是判断该不该用它的 gut check。
免费额度只覆盖很小的用量，千万级写入早就远远超出这个范围。
optionExplanations_en: This is off by three orders of magnitude from what ten million writes per second actually costs.
This is still off by two orders of magnitude -- nowhere near the real bill at that write volume.
Ten million WCUs times $0.00065 per hour times 24 hours lands in six figures -- this math is the gut check for whether the load is even feasible.
The free tier only covers a tiny volume, and ten-million-per-second writes blow far past it.

scenario: 读多写少的 DynamoDB 应用想加缓存把读延迟降到微秒级，同时尽量不引入新的第三方组件。
scenario_en: A read-heavy DynamoDB app wants to add caching to push read latency down to microseconds, while avoiding introducing a new third-party component if possible.
q: 最顺手的方案是？
q_en: What's the most convenient option?
options: 自建 Memcached 集群
DAX，专属缓存微秒响应。
把数据全量导入应用内存
开启强一致读
why: DAX 是 DynamoDB 专用内存缓存，读多且访问模式贴合 DynamoDB API 时可拿到很低延迟，并减少自行维护 Redis/Memcached 的复杂度。它不是通用缓存，强一致读也不能靠 DAX 提速。
why_en: DAX is DynamoDB's purpose-built in-memory cache that delivers microsecond reads without adding a general-purpose cache like Redis.
whenOtherWins: 如果缓存还要服务 DynamoDB 之外的数据、或要用丰富数据结构（排行榜、pub/sub），通用的 Redis 更合适。
options_en: Self-host a Memcached cluster.
DAX, a purpose-built cache with microsecond response.
Load the entire dataset into application memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 专属的内存缓存服务，提供微秒级读延迟。

optionExplanations: 双写引入了「两次写入部分失败」的经典一致性风险，还得自己写补偿逻辑。
两次重建之间用户搜到的都是旧数据，全量重建本身也很耗资源，实时性差。
ES 和 DynamoDB 是两套独立系统，查询协议和数据模型完全不同，不存在这种直连方式。
让 DynamoDB 保持权威数据源、ES 跟着 Streams 事件走，避免应用层维护两份写逻辑，也比全量重建更及时。
optionExplanations_en: Double-writing introduces the classic 'one of two writes partially fails' consistency risk, plus you have to build your own compensation logic.
Between rebuilds users search against stale data, and a full rebuild itself burns significant resources -- poor freshness.
Elasticsearch and DynamoDB are separate systems with entirely different query protocols and data models -- no such direct link exists.
Keeping DynamoDB authoritative with Elasticsearch following Streams events avoids duplicating write logic in the app, and stays fresher than a full rebuild.

q: 为什么在面试里 DynamoDB「几乎可以胜任任何持久层」？（多选）
q_en: Why is DynamoDB 'good for nearly any persistence layer' in an interview? (select all)
options: 高可扩展、高持久
支持 ACID 事务（含跨表）
单毫秒级延迟，配 DAX 可到微秒级
自带 DAX 缓存和 Streams，方便做低延迟读与异步派生视图/CDC
免费且无供应商锁定
why: 扩展、事务、低延迟、附带缓存与 CDC——这套组合覆盖很多持久层需求；但 DAX/Streams 分别是缓存和异步变更流，不提供跨存储强一致，且 DynamoDB 不免费、也深度绑定 AWS。
why_en: DynamoDB pairs high scalability and durability with transactions and single-digit-millisecond latency, though it is not free and still ties you to AWS.
options_en: Highly scalable and highly durable.
Supports ACID transactions, including across tables.
Single-digit-millisecond latency, down to microseconds with DAX.
Ships with DAX caching and Streams, making low-latency reads and async derived views or CDC easy.
Free and has no vendor lock-in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专给 DynamoDB 用的全托管「内存缓存」,挡在 DynamoDB 前面:命中的读从毫秒降到微秒级、还省 RCU。是「加速读」的缓存,不是变更流
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator) is a fully-managed in-memory cache in front of DynamoDB: cached reads drop from milliseconds to microseconds and save RCUs. It is a read cache, not a change stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的 CDC:把每次 item 的增/改/删按顺序变成一串变更事件,供下游(Lambda/Kinesis)实时消费——用来做异步派生视图(更新搜索索引、维护聚合、复制、触发通知)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams is CDC: every item insert/update/delete becomes an ordered stream of change events for downstream consumers (Lambda/Kinesis) to build async derived views (search index, aggregates, replication, notifications).

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 支持 ACID 事务(TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems):可对多个 item(含跨表)原子写入,要么全成要么全回滚。预订/下单可一步原子完成,不必自己写 saga 补偿。代价:2 倍容量、单事务最多 100 item
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB supports ACID transactions (TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems): atomically write multiple items, even across tables, all-or-nothing. Booking/order flows become one atomic step with no manual saga. Cost: 2x capacity, up to 100 items per transaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获数据库的变更(增/改/删)并变成一串事件、供下游实时消费的机制——下游不用轮询,DB 把变更「推」出来。常用来把变更喂给 Elasticsearch 建索引、维护物化视图、复制数据。DynamoDB Streams、Debezium(读 MySQL/PG 的 binlog/WAL)都是 CDC
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC (Change Data Capture) captures a database inserts/updates/deletes as a stream of events for downstream real-time consumption — no polling; the DB pushes its changes. Often used to feed Elasticsearch, maintain materialized views, or replicate. DynamoDB Streams and Debezium (MySQL/PG binlog/WAL) are CDC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 别混:DAX=缓存,加速「读」(毫秒→微秒);Streams=CDC,把「写/变更」变成事件流给下游。一个管读得快、一个管变更传播,方向不同
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Do not confuse: DAX is a cache that speeds up reads (ms→μs); Streams is CDC that turns writes/changes into an event stream for downstream. One is read speed, the other is change propagation.

tradeoff: 全托管强能力 vs 成本与供应商锁定的代价
optionExplanations: 扩展和持久是几乎任何持久层都要的底线诉求，DynamoDB 天然满足，不用自己搭分片方案。
跨表原子写入让预订、下单这类场景不必自己实现补偿逻辑。
默认单毫秒级延迟已经很快，配 DAX 还能进一步压到微秒级，覆盖大部分低延迟诉求。
不用额外引入 Redis 做缓存，也不用自建 CDC 管道去同步搜索索引或做实时分析。
这把「功能强大」和「免费无锁定」混为一谈了，DynamoDB 是收费的托管服务，且深度绑定 AWS。
optionExplanations_en: Scalability and durability are baseline needs for almost any persistence layer, and DynamoDB meets them natively without hand-rolling sharding.
Atomic cross-table writes mean booking or checkout flows don't need their own compensation logic.
The default single-digit-millisecond latency is already fast, and DAX pushes it further down to microseconds, covering most low-latency needs.
No need to bring in Redis separately for caching or build a custom CDC pipeline to sync search indexes or feed real-time analytics.
This conflates 'feature-rich' with 'free and lock-in-free' -- DynamoDB is a paid managed service deeply tied to AWS.
scenario: 面试里为一个已在 AWS 上的新系统选主存储，规模、低延迟、事务需求都有。
scenario_en: In an interview you're picking the primary datastore for a new AWS system with scale, low latency, and transactions.

q: 哪些情况会让你不选 DynamoDB？（多选）
q_en: Which situations should make you avoid DynamoDB? (select all)
options: 成本：每秒几十万写的高量负载下，按读写计费可能贵得离谱
复杂查询：需要 JOIN、ad-hoc 聚合等灵活查询能力
建模信号：发现自己频繁依赖大量 GSI/LSI——说明关系型（如 PostgreSQL）可能更合适
供应商锁定：面试官要求保持 vendor-neutral
需要毫秒级读延迟
why: 四大不选理由：成本、查询灵活性、建模约束（索引泛滥是换关系库的信号）、AWS 锁定。毫秒级延迟恰恰是它的强项，不是短板。
why_en: Avoid DynamoDB for cost-heavy write volumes, complex query needs, index-heavy modeling better served by Postgres, or when vendor neutrality is required.
options_en: Cost: at hundreds of thousands of writes per second, pay-per-request billing can get absurdly expensive.
Complex queries: the system needs joins or ad-hoc aggregation that flexible querying provides.
A modeling signal: leaning on a pile of GSIs and LSIs suggests a relational database like PostgreSQL may fit better.
Vendor lock-in: the interviewer wants a vendor-neutral, open-source choice.
Needing millisecond-level read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引：分区键与主表不同，独立物理分区，只支持最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Global Secondary Index has its own partition key and its own physical partitions, and it only supports eventually consistent reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Local Secondary Index shares the table's partition key but uses a different sort key, and is co-located with the base table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持 JOIN 和灵活查询，是 DynamoDB 建模复杂时的常见替代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database that supports joins and flexible queries, a common alternative when DynamoDB modeling gets too complex.

tradeoff: 键值建模的高效 vs 关系型查询的灵活
optionExplanations: 几十万写/秒的量级下，按请求计费可能高到不现实，这时候要重新算一笔账。
DynamoDB 支持跨表事务，但没有 SQL 式的灵活联表和即席聚合能力，复杂报表类查询会很吃力。
索引堆到七八个说明访问模式本质上是关系型的，硬撑不如直接换库。
有些面试官明确要求避免绑定单一云厂商，这时该考虑开源的替代方案。
这把它的强项当成了弱项——毫秒甚至微秒级（配 DAX）延迟恰恰是选它的理由，不是避开它的理由。
optionExplanations_en: At hundreds of thousands of writes per second, pay-per-request billing can get unrealistically expensive, worth re-running the numbers.
DynamoDB supports cross-table transactions but lacks SQL-style flexible joins and ad-hoc aggregation, so complex reporting queries get painful.
Piling on seven or eight indexes signals the access patterns are fundamentally relational -- better to switch databases than force it.
Some interviewers explicitly want to avoid single-vendor lock-in, which points toward open-source alternatives.
This turns a strength into a weakness -- millisecond, even microsecond with DAX, latency is a reason to pick it, not avoid it.
scenario: 一个跑在 DynamoDB 上的后台，报表要做多表 JOIN 和临时聚合，写入量也在飙升。
scenario_en: A backend on DynamoDB now needs multi-table joins and ad-hoc aggregation, and write volume is climbing fast.

scenario: 设计过程中发现：为了支撑各种查询，一张 DynamoDB 表上已经挂了七八个 GSI 和多个 LSI。
scenario_en: While designing the system, you notice a DynamoDB table already carries seven or eight GSIs plus several LSIs to support various queries.
q: 这个信号说明什么？
q_en: What does this signal mean?
options: 说明设计很成功，索引建得越多查询就越灵活越好
应该把所有查询改成 Scan
访问模式关系化，超出键值建模舒适区。
应该删掉所有索引
why: DynamoDB 要求围绕少数明确访问模式精心建模；索引堆到这个程度说明查询需求本质上是关系型的，硬撑不如换关系库。
why_en: Leaning heavily on many GSIs and LSIs signals relational access patterns that a database like PostgreSQL would serve better.
whenOtherWins: 若只是两三个清晰的次要访问模式，正常使用 GSI/LSI 完全合理，不必换库。
options_en: The design is a success -- the more indexes you build, the more flexible the queries.
Every query should be switched to a Scan.
The access patterns are relational, past key-value modeling's comfort zone.
All the indexes should simply be deleted.
tradeoff: 硬撑键值建模的索引堆积 vs 换用关系库的灵活查询

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引：分区键与主表不同，独立物理分区，只支持最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Global Secondary Index has its own partition key and its own physical partitions, and it only supports eventually consistent reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Local Secondary Index shares the table's partition key but uses a different sort key, and is co-located with the base table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持 JOIN 和灵活查询，是 DynamoDB 建模复杂时的常见替代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database that supports joins and flexible queries, a common alternative when DynamoDB modeling gets too complex.

optionExplanations: 索引越多通常意味着写入时要多付好几倍的维护开销、运维和账单一起被拖累，不是越多越好。
把所有查询都换成 Scan 会让每次查询代价随表增长线性上升，是明显的反模式，跟索引堆积的问题无关。
索引堆到七八个说明查询需求本质上已经关系化了，超出了键值建模能舒服覆盖的范围，这时候该考虑换关系库而不是硬撑。
如果这些查询模式仍是真实需求，删掉索引只会让它们变得低效或彻底不可用，治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: More indexes usually means paying several times the write-time maintenance overhead, dragging down operations and cost -- not simply better.
Switching every query to a Scan makes each query's cost grow linearly with the table, a clear anti-pattern unrelated to the actual index-pileup problem.

Piling up to seven or eight indexes means the query needs have effectively gone relational, past what key-value modeling can comfortably cover -- time to consider a relational database instead of forcing it.
If those query patterns are still genuinely needed, deleting the indexes only makes them inefficient or unusable -- treating the symptom, not the cause.

q: 把「选用 DynamoDB」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for 'choosing DynamoDB' in the correct order:
steps: 代价：按量计费在超高写入下昂贵、查询灵活性差、绑定 AWS
需求：海量数据 + 高可用 + 低延迟，团队不想管运维
缓解：围绕访问模式精心建模、控制索引数量、用估算核对成本
决定性属性：全托管、自动分片扩缩、单毫秒延迟、支持事务
why: 决策链：需求（大规模+免运维）→ 决定性属性（托管、自动扩展、事务）→ 选 DynamoDB → 代价（成本/查询/锁定）→ 缓解（建模+成本估算）。
why_en: Massive scale with no ops burden points to DynamoDB's managed auto-scaling and transactions, whose cost and query limits are mitigated by careful modeling and estimation.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Access patterns known"] --> K["design PK and SK"]
    K --> I["add GSI or LSI only if needed"]
    I --> C["choose consistency per path"]
    C --> S["check hot keys and cost"]
tradeoff: 全托管免运维 vs 成本/查询灵活性/供应商锁定的代价

q: 补全「一致性按路径拆分」这条 DynamoDB 推理：
q_en: Fill in this DynamoDB reasoning about splitting consistency by path:
text: 预订/下单这类关键路径用 {{ConsistentRead=true}} 的强一致读（走 {{leader}} 节点、消耗 2 倍 RCU）；读多、延迟敏感的路径默认{{最终}}一致（任意副本可服务、0.5 RCU/4KB）。
why: 按请求可调一致性让一个系统里两类路径各取所需：正确性优先的花钱买强一致，性能优先的享受默认的便宜和快。
why_en: Critical paths request strongly consistent reads from the leader at double cost while latency-sensitive paths keep the cheap eventually consistent default.
tradeoff: 强一致读的正确性优先 vs 最终一致读的性能优先

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读的一致性开关。默认 false=最终一致(任意副本服务、可能读到略旧、0.5 RCU/4KB);设 true=强一致(必须读 leader 副本、保证最新、1 RCU/4KB=2倍)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB read consistency flag. Default false = eventually consistent (any replica, may be slightly stale, 0.5 RCU/4KB); true = strongly consistent (must read the leader replica, latest data, 1 RCU/4KB = double).

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读容量单位。1 RCU=每秒一次强一致读(≤4KB)=每秒两次最终一致读(≤4KB)。所以强一致读花 1 RCU、最终一致只花 0.5 RCU→强一致=2倍成本
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read Capacity Unit. 1 RCU = one strongly-consistent read/sec (≤4KB) = two eventually-consistent reads/sec; a strong read costs 1 RCU, an eventual read 0.5 — strong is 2x.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 每个 item 存多个副本(通常 3 个跨 AZ),其中一个是 leader:写先落 leader 再复制给 follower。强一致读必须读 leader(它一定有最新写);最终一致读可读任意副本(follower 可能略滞后→读到旧值)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB stores each item on multiple replicas (usually 3 across AZs); one is the leader — writes hit it first, then replicate. A strongly consistent read must read the leader (it has the latest write); an eventually consistent read may read any replica (a follower may lag).

q: 在「分区内索引结构」上，DynamoDB 与 Cassandra 的对比是？
q_en: On 'in-partition index structure', how do DynamoDB and Cassandra compare?
options: 两者都用 LSM 树
前者 B-tree，后者 LSM（写优化）。
DynamoDB 用 LSM，Cassandra 用 B-tree
两者都不用索引
why: DynamoDB 走 B-tree 路线（读写均衡、范围查询高效），Cassandra 走 LSM 路线（极致写吞吐）——同为宽列/键值家族但存储引擎哲学不同。
why_en: DynamoDB indexes each partition with a B-tree by sort key while Cassandra relies on an LSM tree optimized for writes.
options_en: Both use LSM trees.
The former uses a B-tree, the latter a write-optimized LSM tree.
DynamoDB uses LSM, Cassandra uses a B-tree.
Neither uses any index structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平衡树索引结构，支持高效的有序遍历和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced tree index that supports efficient ordered traversal and range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化的树形存储结构：先写内存再顺序刷盘合并，Cassandra 等系统使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized storage structure that buffers writes in memory and merges them to disk sequentially.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源宽列存储数据库，分区内用 LSM 树、面向高写入吞吐设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is an open-source wide-column database that uses LSM trees internally and is optimized for high write throughput.

tradeoff: DynamoDB 读写均衡的 B-tree vs Cassandra 写优化的 LSM
scenario: 对比 DynamoDB 和 Cassandra 在分区内部索引结构上的设计差异。
scenario_en: Comparing how DynamoDB and Cassandra each structure the index inside a partition.
optionExplanations: DynamoDB 分区内部实际走的是 B-tree 路线，不是 LSM，这个说法混淆了两者的存储引擎哲学。
DynamoDB 选 B-tree 换来读写均衡和高效范围查询，Cassandra 选 LSM 换来极致写吞吐，同属宽列/键值家族但存储引擎的取舍方向不同。
这把两者的存储引擎选型完全对调了，方向说反了。
两者其实都有精心设计的索引结构，只是选择的路线不同，说没有索引不成立。
optionExplanations_en: DynamoDB's partitions actually take the B-tree route, not LSM, so this conflates the two systems' storage-engine philosophies.

DynamoDB's B-tree route trades for balanced read/write and efficient range queries, while Cassandra's LSM route trades for maximum write throughput -- same wide-column/key-value family, different storage philosophy.
This swaps the two systems' storage-engine choices entirely -- the direction is reversed.
Both actually have carefully designed index structures, just different routes -- claiming neither uses indexing doesn't hold.

q: DynamoDB 的 attribute 支持哪些类型形态？
q_en: What type shapes does a DynamoDB attribute support?
options: 只支持字符串一种标量类型
只支持数字和布尔两种类型
标量、集合与嵌套结构皆支持
只支持二进制大对象存储
why: attribute 是键值对，类型覆盖标量、集合、嵌套结构（如地址对象），因此单个 item 就能表达相当复杂的文档数据。
why_en: Attributes support scalar and set types and can be nested, allowing complex document structures within a single item.
options_en: Only the string scalar type is supported.
Only numbers and booleans are supported.
Scalars, sets, and nested structures are all supported.
Only binary large objects can be stored.
scenario: 设计一张表的 item，要决定字段该用哪些数据类型表示。
scenario_en: Designing an item's fields for a table and deciding which data types to use.
optionExplanations: 数字、布尔、集合、嵌套对象都同样支持，不止字符串这一种类型。
这遗漏了字符串和各类集合类型，它们同样是一等公民。
标量、集合类型都支持，还能嵌套表达地址对象这类复杂结构，单个 item 就能像小型文档。
这把二进制当成了唯一支持的形态，实际标量和集合类型同样原生支持，不需要都转成二进制。
optionExplanations_en: Numbers, booleans, sets, and nested objects are all equally supported, not just strings.
This misses strings and every set type, which are equally first-class.
Scalars and sets are both supported, and nesting can express complex structures like an address object -- a single item can act like a small document.
This treats binary as the only supported shape, when scalars and sets are natively supported too, with no need to convert to binary.

q: 把多数读设为最终一致读，在读容量（RCU）成本上有什么好处？
q_en: What read-capacity (RCU) cost benefit comes from making most reads eventually consistent?
options: 最终一致读省一半读容量。
两种读消耗完全相同，这个选择不影响成本
最终一致读免费，完全不计入读容量
只有强一致读会消耗读容量，最终一致读不计费
why: 最终一致读 0.5 RCU/4KB、强一致读 1 RCU/4KB；把大部分只读流量放在最终一致路径上，能直接把这部分读成本砍半。
why_en: Eventually consistent reads cost half the RCUs of strongly consistent reads, so routing most read-only traffic through the eventual path directly halves that read cost.
scenario: 一个读多写少的服务把 90% 的读请求设为最终一致，只有下单确认页强制走强一致读。
scenario_en: A read-heavy service sets 90% of reads to eventual consistency, forcing strong consistency only on the order-confirmation page.
options_en: An eventually consistent read saves half the read capacity.
Strong and eventual reads consume exactly the same amount, so this choice does not affect cost.
Eventually consistent reads are free and never count against read capacity.
Only strongly consistent reads consume read capacity; eventual reads are not billed at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读容量单位：一个 RCU 每秒最多读 4KB（强一致 1 次或最终一致 2 次）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读请求里的参数，设为 true 即要求强一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ConsistentRead is a per-request parameter that, when set to true, requires a strongly consistent read.

optionExplanations: 最终一致读每 4KB 只算半个 RCU，强一致读要算满 1 个，把大部分只读流量导到最终一致路径就能把这部分读成本直接砍半。
两者的计费系数其实不同，选哪种一致性会直接影响读容量账单，说完全相同不成立。
最终一致读同样要消耗读容量，只是单价减半，不是完全免费。
最终一致读依然计费，只是单价是强一致读的一半，不是不计费。
optionExplanations_en: An eventually consistent read costs just 0.5 RCU per 4KB versus 1 RCU for strong consistency, so routing most read-only traffic through the eventual path directly halves that read cost.
The two are actually billed at different rates, so which consistency you pick does change the read-capacity bill -- claiming no difference doesn't hold.
Eventually consistent reads still consume read capacity, just at half the rate -- not free.
Eventually consistent reads are still billed, just at half the strong-read rate, not zero.

q: 选分区键时除了匹配查询模式，还必须考虑什么？
q_en: Besides matching the query pattern, what else must you consider when choosing a partition key?
options: 分区键取值在字母表里的先后排列顺序
让数据均匀分布，避免热点分区。
分区键必须是数字
分区键越长越好
why: 分区键的两大准则：服务最常见查询 + 均匀分布。倾斜的分区键会造出热点分区，单分区吞吐上限一到就出现节流。
why_en: A good partition key both serves common queries and spreads data evenly, since a hot partition throttles at the per-partition throughput limits.
options_en: The alphabetical ordering position of the partition key's values.
Distribute data evenly to avoid hot partitions.
The partition key must be numeric.
The longer the partition key, the better.
optionExplanations: 分区键哈希后决定物理位置，跟字母顺序毫无关系。
除了服务最常见查询，还要看取值的基数和访问频率够不够分散，否则某个键值扎堆写入会让单个分区先撞上吞吐天花板、率先被限流。
字符串、数字都能做分区键，只要哈希后分布均匀，不存在类型限制。
决定分布是否均匀的是取值的基数和访问频率，不是分区键字符串的长度。
optionExplanations_en: A partition key's hash determines its physical location -- alphabetical order has nothing to do with it.

Beyond serving the common query, check whether the value's cardinality and access frequency spread out enough -- a skewed key creates hot partitions that throttle once they hit the per-partition throughput ceiling.
Both strings and numbers can serve as partition keys as long as their hashes distribute evenly -- there's no type restriction.
What determines even distribution is cardinality and access frequency, not the string length of the key.

闭源，只能靠 AWS 文档和论文。
因为内部是用汇编写的
因为 AWS 禁止讨论它

why_en: DynamoDB is not open source, so internals are known only through AWS documentation and the published DynamoDB paper.
options_en: Because it is designed too simply to have any internal mechanics.
Closed source -- understanding relies on AWS docs and the paper.
Because the internals are written in assembly.
Because AWS forbids discussing it.
